mdx.setup.fabric_dependency.message: If it is not installed already, download {fabricApi} and place it in the same folder.

mdx.setup.version_step_viaversion.message: If your server is not running {version}, you will need to install {viaVersion}. For more information, see {supportedVersions}.

mdx.setup.version_step_proxy.message: All servers on the network must accept {version} Java clients, as Geyser imitates one.

mdx.setup.proxy_install_only.message: Install Geyser only on the {proxy} server! You can install Floodgate on all servers for better skin support and network-wide Floodgate API availability for other plugins.

mdx.setup.modded_requirements.message: {jarName} runs only on a {version} server, and only works alongside server-side mods. Mods that players also need to install on their client will not work. See {supportedVersions} for more details.

mdx.setup.self_port_choice.message: Since you are self-hosting, you can choose the port freely; the default is 19132. Geyser uses it over both TCP and UDP, so it cannot be the port of the {platform} server.

mdx.setup.self_port_choice_standalone.message: Since you are self-hosting, you can choose the port freely; the default is 19132. Geyser uses it over both TCP and UDP.

mdx.setup.self_port_sharing.message: {important}: No other program can use the Geyser port, over either protocol. This includes programs that use UDP, such as voice chat mods or Query, and programs that use TCP, such as another server, a web map, or a website.

mdx.setup.connect_local.message: On the same device as the server, connect with {localhost} or {loopback} as the address. Other devices in the same local network can use your local IPv4 address, which starts with {ten} or {oneNineTwo}.

mdx.setup.connect_lan.message: Alternatively, open Minecraft: Bedrock Edition and join the LAN server in the {friends} tab.

mdx.setup.connect_remote.message: To let players from outside your network join, you need to make the Geyser port reachable from the internet.

mdx.setup.connect_tcp_udp.message: The Geyser port has to be forwarded for both TCP and UDP. Before NetherNet, forwarding UDP was enough. Now, players use TCP to find your server and UDP to play on it, so without TCP your server will not show up. If you use the "NetherNet and RakNet" option, also forward the {webrtcPort} for UDP.

mdx.setup.connect_port_forwarding.message: {portForwarding}: open the Geyser port (e.g. 19132) for both TCP and UDP in your router and in your firewall. Players then connect with your public IPv4 address and the port. For detailed steps, see {guide}.

mdx.setup.connect_playit.message: {playit}: if you cannot open a port, or do not want to expose your home IP address, playit.gg can create a tunnel for you. See {guide}. That guide was written for RakNet. For NetherNet, see {status}. Ngrok does not work, since it does not support UDP.

mdx.setup.https_step_title.message: Recommended: Set up HTTPS for signaling

mdx.setup.https_step.message: Geyser's built-in signaling server uses plain HTTP by default, so Minecraft shows players a "Trust on First Use?" prompt the first time they join. To avoid this prompt, serve signaling over HTTPS, as explained in {httpsGuide}. Some external signaling services, such as {warden}, provide HTTPS as well.

mdx.setup.floodgate_info.message: To allow Bedrock Edition players to join your server without a paid Java Edition account, you can use {floodgate}.

mdx.setup.viaproxy_not_plugin.title.message: ViaProxy is not a plugin or mod

mdx.setup.viaproxy_not_plugin.message: ViaProxy is a standalone program that runs separately from your Minecraft server. Do not put the ViaProxy jar into your server's {plugins} or {mods} folder. To run Geyser as a plugin or mod on your server instead, pick your server software in the tabs above.

mdx.setup.viaproxy_accounts.message: If you use the ViaProxy GUI, you can use its account management to join online mode servers with Bedrock Edition. If you use the ViaProxy CLI and want Bedrock players to join your online mode server, install and set up {floodgate}.

mdx.setup.viaproxy_auth_type.message: ViaProxy manages the {authType} setting itself, so its value in the config is ignored.

mdx.setup.standalone_java.message: You need Java 21 or newer to run Geyser. To run Geyser Standalone on Android, see the end of this page.

mdx.setup.standalone_not_plugin.message: Geyser Standalone is not a plugin or mod. It is a separate Java program that runs alongside your Java Edition server.

mdx.setup.standalone_folder.message: Create a new folder for Geyser, and put the jar in it.

mdx.setup.standalone_gui.message: {gui} (recommended): double-click the jar file. Geyser creates all the files it needs.

mdx.setup.standalone_console.message: {console}: create a startup script, like the one you would use for a Paper server. See {startupScript} for what to put into it. Run it, and Geyser creates all the files it needs.

mdx.setup.standalone_remote_intro.message: To choose which Java Edition server Geyser Standalone sends players to, find the {java} section:

mdx.setup.standalone_remote.message: Change {address} to the Java server's address, or leave it as it is if the server runs on the same machine as Geyser. Then change {port} to the Java server's port. Set {authType} to {floodgate} if you set up Floodgate on the Java server, otherwise to {online} for an online mode server or {offline} for an offline mode server. To use Floodgate with Geyser Standalone, see {floodgateSetup}.

mdx.setup.standalone_android_caution.message: Apps such as Termux can run Geyser on Android, but how well this works depends on how powerful your device is. Do so at your own risk.

mdx.setup.standalone_termux_script.message: Alternatively, there is an automated setup script for clean Termux installs. It might not work for everyone, so try it if the steps above do not work:

mdx.setup.https_note.message: Unless signaling runs over {https}, Minecraft asks players whether they trust the server the first time they join.

mdx.setup.open_config_simple.message: Now open the file {configLocation}. Find the part that starts with {bedrock}, and change the lines shown below.

mdx.setup.preconfigured.message: No changes needed. {name} automatically configures Geyser.

mdx.setup.transport_nethernet_simple.message: NetherNet is supported fully by 26.50+. If you'd like to also have working MOTD and player count for older versions, you will need to set up both NetherNet and Raknet.

mdx.setup.transport_both_compat.message: Also accepts RakNet, for additional compatibility: some Bedrock versions, such as 26.40, fetch the server's MOTD and player count over RakNet. This option needs a separate UDP port for NetherNet.

mdx.setup.placeholder_java_port.message: The port of the Java server.

mdx.setup.placeholder_java_port_udp.message: A UDP port for NetherNet, other than {port}. This can be the Java server's port: the Java server only uses it over TCP, so Geyser can use it over UDP. Any other available UDP port works too.

mdx.setup.placeholder_second_available_p.message: An available UDP port for NetherNet, other than {port}. Open it for UDP.

mdx.setup.raknet_on_port.message: RakNet uses {port} over UDP, so that port has to be open for UDP as well.

mdx.setup.summary.supporter_configures.message: {name} configures Geyser for you automatically, including NetherNet.

mdx.setup.unconfirmed_reach_out_update.message: These instructions have not been checked for NetherNet yet. If Bedrock players can't join, reach out to {name} to get instructions on how to use Geyser, and let us know on {discord} so we can update this guide.

mdx.setup.try_not_listed.message: If your host cannot give you a separate port, follow the {notListed} instead. Players then join through {warden}, an external signaling service.

mdx.setup.try_not_listed.link.message: "Not listed" guide for using only the Java server's port

mdx.setup.no_signaling.message: {name} supports neither built-in nor external signaling, so Bedrock players cannot connect over NetherNet.

pages.main.subtitle.message: Enable clients from Minecraft Bedrock Edition to join your Minecraft Java server

components.homepage_features.1.line1.message: Geyser is a program that allows Minecraft: Bedrock Edition clients to join Minecraft: Java Edition servers, allowing for true crossplay between both editions of the game.

components.homepage_features.1.line2.message: The ultimate goal of this project is to allow Minecraft: Bedrock Edition users to join Minecraft: Java Edition servers as seamlessly as possible.

components.homepage_features.2.message: Geyser acts as a translator which sits between the Bedrock client and the Java server. It takes data from the Bedrock client and translates it into a format the Java server understands and vice versa. Geyser works with any modern Minecraft version and can be installed either as a plugin or ran as a standalone program.

components.homepage_features.3.line1.message: Geyser can be joined from Bedrock clients on Windows 10/11, iOS, Android, and even consoles. Geyser works with a wide array of hosting providers, but can also be used as its own standalone proxy to join any Minecraft server!

components.homepage_features.3.line2.message: If you are a server owner, you can install our Floodgate plugin which allows Xbox Live authenticated Bedrock users to join without a Java Edition account!
